name: connectwise-automate
description: ConnectWise Automate (RMM): computers, clients, an interactive computers table, and read/write escape hatches to the Automate REST API.
long_description:
ConnectWise Automate (RMM) as a local MCP server. Search and read computers, list clients, and reach any other Automate endpoint through cw_automate_api_get (GET only) and cw_automate_api_write.

Every tool is named cw_automate_* and shows a Title Case name in the client. Read-only tools carry readOnlyHint; the write escape hatch refuses every call without confirm: true. cw_automate_view_computers renders an interactive agent table on hosts that support MCP Apps. cw_status_server is always registered and reports exactly which fields are still empty.

This bundle runs on your own machine and holds the Automate credentials there. PSA and Control ship as separate bundles from the same repository.

tools.name: Server Status
tools.description: Report which ConnectWise products are configured and what an unconfigured one still needs

tools.name: Get Automate Computer
tools.description: Get one Automate agent in full detail

tools.name: Automate API Get
tools.description: GET any Automate endpoint that has no dedicated tool

tools.name: Automate API Write
tools.description: POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE an Automate endpoint, acting on live RMM agents — writes to ConnectWise

tools.name: View Automate Computers
tools.description: Interactive table of Automate agents: online or offline, OS, client and last contact

automate_password.title: Automate password
automate_password.description: Automate account password. Supply it from your secret manager.

automate_client_id.title: Automate clientId
automate_client_id.description: Automate developer clientId GUID, sent with every Automate request.

automate_totp_secret.title: Automate TOTP secret
automate_totp_secret.description: Only needed when the Automate login account keeps two-factor authentication enabled. Paste the same base32 seed the account's authenticator was enrolled with and the connector generates each passcode itself. The cleaner alternative is a dedicated API service account exempt from two-factor; leave this blank then.
